### [Introducing 100K context windows](https://www.anthropic.com/news/100k-context-windows)

**Anthropic** · 2026-09-09

Anthropic has expanded Claude's context window from 9K to 100K tokens, enabling the model to process roughly 75,000 words in under a minute.

- Context window size increased from 9,000 to 100,000 tokens (approximately 75,000 words or 6 hours of transcribed audio).
- In a benchmark test, Claude-Instant retrieved a modified line inserted into the 72,000-token text of The Great Gatsby in 22 seconds.
- The 100K token capability is accessible directly via Anthropic's API.
- Provides a direct prompt-synthesis alternative to vector search-based approaches for complex document analysis.

**Why it matters:** Businesses can digest, synthesize, and query hundreds of pages of documentation or long-form transcripts in a single prompt without relying on vector search retrieval.

`anthropic` `claude` `llm` `context-window` `api`

### [An AI policy tool for today: Invest in NIST](https://www.anthropic.com/news/an-ai-policy-tool-for-today-ambitiously-invest-in-nist)

**Anthropic** · 2026-09-09

Anthropic proposes that Congress ambitiously increase funding for the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to accelerate the development of AI measurement tools, standards, and safety testbeds.

- Open-ended AI models exhibit unpredictable behaviors and abrupt capabilities, while the field lacks widely-agreed-upon methods to measure and assess associated risks.
- Anthropic identifies NIST funding as a actionable policy tool to create technical standards for AI assurance, complementing broader governance initiatives.
- NIST's historical baseline in AI standards includes the Face Recognition Vendor Test, the AI Risk Management Framework, and the early MNIST handwriting dataset.
- Anthropic cites recent under-resourcing and funding stagnation in NIST's AI-related programs relative to the rapid pace of AI model scaling and deployment.

**Why it matters:** Accurate, standardized measurement tools are a necessary technical prerequisite for objective safety assessments and effective AI regulation.

`ai-policy` `nist` `ai-safety` `governance` `benchmarking`

### [Quoting Calif Research](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Sep/10/calif-research/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-09-10

Calif Research released a demo of WeWorm, the first zero-click worm spreading via WeChat calls across iOS and Android, developed in under two weeks using AI.

- WeWorm executes without requiring the victim to answer or interact with the WeChat call, remaining silent even if answered.
- The vulnerability was identified and a remote code execution (RCE) exploit was authored in approximately two days using AI assistance.
- Developing the full worm required one additional week, significantly accelerating a process that historically took larger teams months.
- Human researchers provided targeted judgment and safe testing protocols, while AI performed the majority of the underlying development work.

**Why it matters:** AI drastically lowers the time and labor required to discover vulnerabilities and engineer cross-platform, zero-click remote code execution exploits.

### [Alberta uses Claude to find and fix security vulnerabilities](https://www.anthropic.com/news/alberta-government-claude-cybersecurity)

**Anthropic** · 2026-09-09

The Government of Alberta used Claude Code with Opus and Sonnet models to scan and remediate 466 million lines of code across 3,400 government repositories in 20 hours.

- Approximately 50 autonomous, parallel Claude Code agents performed a two-stage review: a rules engine flagged known patterns, followed by LLM verification providing exact file and line citations.
- The automated review covered 1,280 applications across 27 provincial ministries, completing an assessment estimated to take 6.5 years via traditional approaches in roughly 20 hours.
- Claude generated patches, wrote missing automated unit tests to verify safety, and modernized legacy codebases, including rebuilding a 25-year-old Java subsidy portal in 4 to 5 days.

**Why it matters:** Demonstrates that parallelized LLM agents can rapidly perform large-scale security auditing, test generation, and legacy codebase refactoring across complex government infrastructure.

`cybersecurity` `claude` `code-auditing` `devsecops` `llm-agents`
